name: Heritage almanac
label: Heritage almanac — rural life, traditions, migrations, land and family stories, arguments built on numbers
blurb: Updated edition: engraved caps on a letterpress plate over moving footage, didone figures, ledger-slip key points, a surveyor's pencil for the notes, state-against-state comparisons, giants-against-dots, dividing districts, index pages, and a plat map with a township grid. Slate ink on oatmeal paper. Slow and calm.
tagline: Engraved caps on a letterpress plate, didone figures, plat maps - slate ink on oatmeal paper.
points: Plat map with a township grid
best_for: rural life, traditions, migrations, land and family stories, arguments built on numbers

devices_summary.use: Chapter heading stamped over MOVING footage: plate stamp, engraved title, pencil note. One per act.
Place cartouche over footage: where we are.
A key point on a ledger slip (punched holes, double keyline) over a dimmed photo.
One figure stamped between two hairlines with a pencil note.
Two things compared row by row (people / places / districts); each value counts up on its own word.
One circle sized by its value beside a field of small dots - one big thing against many small ones.
One cell inside a boundary dividing into 2, 3, 10 - growth by division.
Gazetteer index rows: name, dotted leader, figure; one row highlighted.
Then -> now with an arrow and the difference stamped (2015 -> 2025).
A line drawn across years on paper; each point appears on its words.
A field fenced into equal strips: one whole divided among many.
One bar split into shares that grow in turn: 'more than half...'.
Columns that rise to their values on paper.
A ring of houses around a centre, with roles as tags: a community and its structure.
The animated map: the camera flies between places, pins drop, routes draw, regions light up. Every place the narration names gets one (group nearby places into one map scene).
Depth pop: the subject is cut out of the photo and grows while the ground darkens and blurs. Use when the narration names a real person, place or object - never private people.
Everything but one circle darkens and blurs; a label points at the subject. 'Look here' moments: the detail that matters in a photo.
